einzeiler: Boaz Weinstein discusses private credit, tender offers and closed-end fund activism.
kurzfassung: Boaz Weinstein of Saba Capital Management joins to discuss his tender offers for private BDCs and interval funds at discounts to net asset value. The discussion covers liquidity mismatches in retail private credit, the lessons learned from closed-end fund activism, and the broader risks in private markets. They also examine why managers avoid buying back their own discounted shares and the phenomenon of volatility laundering.
stichpunkte: Saba Capital submitted tender offers for private credit and real estate vehicles like Blue Owl BDCs and Starwood REIT at significant discounts to NAV.
Retail private credit and interval funds have overpromised liquidity to investors whose redemption queues are growing rapidly.
Closed-end fund activism and private credit vehicles share structural similarities under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
Managers resist turning funds into open-ended products or buying back shares at deep discounts to preserve their assets under management and fee income.
Some major managers like Blackstone handled redemptions well by providing liquidity, while others gated funds for multi-year periods.
Private credit valuations face downward pressure from rising default rates, write-downs, and falling SOFR rates.
Digital asset treasury companies present risks of shareholder dilution and high executive compensation without strict 1940 Act protections.

clips.hook: Fire insurance that doesn't work when there's a fire
clips.text: Boaz Weinstein explains the structural similarities and subtle distinctions between closed-end funds and activist investment strategies.
The governance structure of 40 Act products allows boards to dismiss managers, mirroring the oversight mechanisms found in closed-end funds.
Applying leverage to a portfolio effectively halves the discount on assets, turning a 30 percent price drop into a 15 percent reduction for the investor.
Rising default rates and net asset value adjustments create significant pressure on real estate investment trusts, despite Blackstone's efforts to stabilize the BREIT vehicle.
The debate surrounding private credit valuation highlights concerns over monthly mark-to-market practices and the historical risks of high Sharpe ratios.

beschreibung:
Matt and Katie talked in March to Boaz Weinstein of Saba Capital Management about his tenders for OBDC II and SREIT, semi-liquid fund liquidity, reflexivity, the lure of permanent capital, private credit NAVs, public vs. private BDC discounts, preserving brand value, volatility laundering, howling at the moon, bowling and, why not, DATs.
